_comment: Single source of truth for every THIRD-PARTY upstream that romdev's build
scripts fetch + compile to WASM. romdev does NOT vendor any of this source
into git — it is fetched on demand by the build scripts, cached under build/
(gitignored), patched with OUR patches (scripts/patches/, committed, ours),
and only the resulting .wasm artifacts ship in the packages.
Edit a pin HERE, never in a build-*.sh. Each build script reads this via
kind: 'git'  -> fetched with `git` at the pinned commit (shallow).
kind: 'tarball' -> fetched with curl; 'sha256' lets the build detect drift.
'ref' is a human label (tag/branch); 'commit' is the EXACT pin that builds.
'license' records who owns the upstream code — it is theirs, not ours; we
ship only built artifacts and our own patches.
The toolchain image itself is pinned separately: build-image/Dockerfile
(emscripten/emsdk:4.0.18). WASM is not bit-reproducible across emcc versions,
so an emsdk bump is a deliberate change.

vasm68k.version: rolling (sha-pinned 2026-05-29; upstream tarball carries no version label)
vasm68k.note: Upstream serves only a rolling 'latest' tarball with no version in the URL. sha256 is our only drift detector — fill it after the next clean build and treat a mismatch as a deliberate bump.

maxmod.note: GBA music/sound library (libmm.a). Built with the native arm-none-eabi toolchain; see build-maxmod.sh.

mmutil.note: Host-side soundbank converter (.xm/.mod/.it/.s3m → maxmod binary). Built as a native Linux ELF, paired with maxmod.

sgdk.note: Sega Genesis SDK. We build its sjasm (Z80 assembler) + bintos (Z80-blob->m68k embed) tools to WASM (build-sjasm.sh) and compile the SGDK runtime + sound drivers from source.

armips.note: Assembler for the N64 RSP microcode a decomp project rebuilds from source. Built to WASM by build-armips.sh with std::filesystem (no ext/filesystem submodule); ships in romdev-toolchain-ido beside the other decomp build tools. The commit N64 decomp projects' armips install scripts pin.

kmc_gcc.note: gcc 2.7.2 as N64 SDK (KMC) decomp projects compile with: the driver, cccp and cc1, built to WASM by build-decomp-gcc.sh into romdev-toolchain-decomp-gcc (wasm/kmc-2.7.2/).

kmc_binutils.note: The binutils 2.6 assembler (with --force-n64align) paired with KMC gcc 2.7.2; built to WASM by build-decomp-gcc.sh.

egcs_gcc.note: EGCS 1.1.2 (gcc 2.91.66) for mips-linux, the compiler N64 decomp projects build their iQue (China) versions with: driver, cccp and cc1, built to WASM by build-decomp-gcc.sh egcs into romdev-toolchain-decomp-gcc (wasm/egcs-1.1.2/).

egcs_binutils.note: The binutils 2.9.5 assembler paired with EGCS 1.1.2; built to WASM by build-decomp-gcc.sh egcs. The reference assembler is an x86_64 Linux binary using glibc obstacks; the patch lays obstack chunks and frags out and sizes new chunks as there, so gas splits frags (and folds label differences in .mdebug stabs) at the same places.

slinky_cli.note: decompals' linker-script generator, the release N64 decomp projects download as tools/slinky/slinky-cli. Built to WASM (wasm32-unknown-emscripten) by build-decomp-rust-tools.sh; ships in romdev-toolchain-decomp-gcc (wasm/tools/).

pigment64.note: decompals' PNG to N64 texture converter (tools/pigment64/pigment64 in decomp projects). Built to WASM by build-decomp-rust-tools.sh; ships in romdev-toolchain-decomp-gcc (wasm/tools/).

crunch64_cli.note: decompals' N64 compression library (gzip/yay0/yaz0/mio0) behind a CLI; the same crunch64 release decomp projects' Python ROM compressors call. Built to WASM by build-decomp-rust-tools.sh; ships in romdev-toolchain-decomp-gcc (wasm/tools/).

ido_static_recomp.license: ido-static-recomp: MIT (recompiler); IRIX IDO binaries it translates: see ido/<ver>/LICENSE.md upstream
ido_static_recomp.note: IDO 5.3 + 7.1 statically recompiled to C by the pinned recomp, then compiled to WASM by build-ido.sh; ships via romdev-toolchain-ido. Same commit the decompals N64 projects pin as their submodule.

heavy_toolchains._comment: GCC-family cross-toolchains — NOT covered by the light build image; need a native cross-gcc bootstrap. Pins recorded for completeness.

binutils_mips_linux.note: binutils for target mips-linux-gnu (the traditional-MIPS ELF vectors N64 decomp projects assemble, link and objcopy with). Built to WASM by build-mips-linux-binutils-wasm.sh; ships as mips-linux-gnu-{as,ld,objcopy,objdump} in romdev-toolchain-mips-gcc. The mips-elf tools cannot stand in: their IRIX-compatible vector names section symbols in .strtab and reorders symbols, so objects differ byte-for-byte.

gcc_mips_linux.note: gcc for target mips-linux-gnu (driver, cpp, cc1), the modern cross gcc N64 decomp projects compile data-only TUs and preprocess .s files and linker scripts with. Built to WASM by build-mips-linux-gcc-wasm.sh with Debian/Ubuntu's target configuration; ships in romdev-toolchain-decomp-gcc (wasm/mips-linux-gnu-14.2/). Same gcc release as romdev-toolchain-mips-gcc's cc1.

binutils.note: binutils-2.42. Built to WASM for THREE targets: m68k-elf (Genesis: build-m68k-wasm-tools.sh), arm-none-eabi (GBA: build-arm-wasm-tools.sh), and z80-elf (SMS/GG/MSX/GB/GBC disassembly+reassembly: build-z80-binutils-wasm.sh — one z80-elf serves both Z80 and gbz80 via -march/-m). Each ships as/ld/objcopy/objdump.

analysis._comment: RE analysis engine (CFG/xrefs/functions; decompiler in phase 3). Built by build-rizin.sh, ships via romdev-analysis.

rz-ghidra._comment: Phase 3: Ghidra C++ decompiler via rz-ghidra. Not built yet.

sleigh_specs._comment: External Ghidra SLEIGH specs for the 3 CPUs stock Ghidra lacks (SM83/65816/HuC6280). Compiled to .sla by build-decompiler.sh; only the compiled .sla ships, never the .slaspec source.

ghidra_snes.author: Arnaud 'red' Rouyer (joshleaves), 65816 spec derived from ghidra-65816

ghidra_huc6280.licenseNote: No LICENSE file in the repo, BUT the spec is a DERIVATIVE of Ghidra's own Apache-2.0 6502.slaspec — git history shows it was developed inside Ghidra/Processors/6502/ then moved to HuC6280/ (PR #1 'Remove 6502 dependencies'); the header + register layout match 6502.slaspec near-verbatim. Apache-2.0 flows down to derivatives and cannot be revoked by a downstream author. Shipped as Apache-2.0 with attribution to the Ghidra/NSA project + Jozsef Tikviczki (TiCoKH) + qufb. Only the compiled .sla ships.
ghidra_huc6280.author: Jozsef Tikviczki (TiCoKH); base from Ghidra/NSA (Apache-2.0); cleanup by qufb
